answer: Registration pins each identity to one atlas coordinate, where a cedar strip swells and shrinks with local humidity. Each identity keeps one strip and a live sensor there all epoch. At unpredictable beacon times, verifiers demand the current length within ten seconds and check it against the weather model for that coordinate and minute. A reading the model cannot reproduce is a fable and earns zero; two identities reporting one series are exposed as one site. One honest agent maintains one strip; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 strips at 1,000 coordinates, because one site yields only one curve.
